findings.problem: The three steps never seated a filter, put the coffee in the basket, read the spent grounds or set a holding window, so a trained person could not make the pot from them in order.
findings.change: Six steps: rinse the airpot hot and seat a paper filter; weigh about 60 g a litre into the filter and level the bed; brew the basket's size; run it into the sealed airpot and write the brew time; read the spent grounds; sell within 30 to 60 minutes and never top an old pot up (Library: Batch brew is the one that pays; Batch Brew card).

findings.problem: Said nothing of when it goes to the table.
findings.change: Added: It is the coffee for brunch, a banquet or a whole table at once (Batch Brew card, Sells to).

findings.problem: "A guest who says burnt is usually tasting a pot left on heat" contradicts the Library: the faults lesson "Sour, and the word the guest will use instead" says an under-extracted cup comes back called burnt, while the Over-extracted card ties "stewed" and "bottom of the pot" to a held pot.
A temperature in Fahrenheit without Celsius (style; schema languageProblems).
The answer "60 g per litre, just under 1:17" was the longest option and the only one with two figures, a length clue; "About 33 g per litre" is not a choice a trained person makes.
findings.change: Options now "18 g in, 36 g out", "About 45 g per litre", "About 60 g per litre", "About 80 g per litre"; the explanation names 18 g in, 36 g out as espresso.
